svg.title: A client with a traumatic brain injury and an ICP of 24 mmHg receives IV mannitol. Two hours later, which finding best tells the nurse the drug is having its intended effect?
svg.desc: Mannitol pulls fluid off the brain and that fluid is excreted, so increased urine output is how the nurse confirms it is working. The other three findings together are Cushing's triad — a late herniation sign meaning the ICP is still climbing, so they show the opposite of the intended effect.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Neurologic Dysfunction &
Cerebrovascular Disorders
Read the situation
A client with a traumatic brain injury and
an ICP of 24 mmHg receives IV mannitol.
Two hours later, which finding best tells
the nurse the drug is having its intended
effect?
What fits here
A marked increase in urine output
Why it fits
Mannitol pulls fluid off the brain and
that fluid is excreted, so increased urine
output is how the nurse confirms it is
working. The other three findings together
are Cushing's triad — a late herniation
sign meaning the ICP is still climbing, so
they show the opposite of the intended
effect.
